commits: 06a2b85 A folder opened without settings compiles with the engine its preamble's packages need, unless a % !TEX program names one
e320549 session_add_package loads a package after the main file's last \usepackage, in the open document's edits or on disk, unless it loads it already
ad0c27c A build asked for runs until it ends or is stopped; only an automatic one is stopped after three minutes
5a9cfc7 A build's errors and warnings explain what TeX's message means and offer one fix a host runs as any command, in place of missing
contract:
Written in docs/core-api.md (session commands table, session_compile row, install_package row, build_finished row, and a new "Explanations and fixes" subsection under Events).

1. Build items: every LogItem in build_finished's result.errors and result.warnings, and the `issue` that session_issue and session_choose_issue answer, now has two new fields. The `missing` field is gone.
   - `explain`: a string or null. It is one or two plain sentences, for the build panel under the message.
   - `fix`: null or {title, help, command, args, confirm?}.
   A host shows `fix` as a button titled `title`, with `help` as its tooltip, and knows no fix by name. On a click:
   - When `confirm` is present, ask first with its text; Cancel does nothing.
   - Call `command` with `args` through tl_call_async, adding `session` for a session_* command.
   - An error answer is shown as that command's would be, and stops there.
   - Otherwise apply the answer's `edits`, if any, exactly as session_replace's (the open document's edits at its `version`).
   - Then call session_compile (a manual build).
   The four fixes, for example:
   - Install: {"title":"Install","help":"Installs the TeX Live package that has foo.sty, then compiles again.","command":"install_package","args":{"file":"foo.sty"}}. Comes from a missing .sty/.cls, and replaces the old `missing` field.
   - Add package: {"title":"Add \\usepackage{graphicx}","help":"Loads graphicx in the main file's preamble, then compiles again.","command":"session_add_package","args":{"name":"graphicx"}}. Offered for an undefined command or environment in the catalogue's map, and only while the main file doesn't load that package.
   - Use XeLaTeX: {"title":"Use XeLaTeX",...,"command":"session_set_settings","args":{"patch":{"engine":"xelatex"}}}. Offered for a Unicode character pdfLaTeX can't set up, or for fontspec, unicode-math, polyglossia or xeCJK needing XeTeX or LuaTeX.
   - Turn On Shell Escape: {"title":"Turn On Shell Escape",...,"command":"session_set_settings","args":{"patch":{"shellEscape":true}},"confirm":"Shell Escape lets this document run programs on your computer as it compiles. Turn it on only for documents you trust."}. Goes on the existing SHELL_ESCAPE error.
   The args for session_set_settings are {patch:{...}}, because that command takes `patch`.

2. New session command: session_add_package {session, name} -> {edits, written}, the same shape as session_replace.
   - It puts `\usepackage{name}` on a line of its own at the end of the line where the main file's last \usepackage argument ends, or else after \documentclass's line.
   - If the main file is open, nothing is written: `edits` is {path, version, edits:[{start, length:0, text:"\n\\usepackage{name}"}]} and `written` is [].
   - If it isn't open, the file is written through the same replace_in_files path, giving written [{file, count:1}].
   - If the main file already loads the package (\usepackage or \RequirePackage, not in a comment), or has no \documentclass, nothing changes: {edits:null, written:[]}.
   - It answers 409 as session_replace does while a change on disk is unsettled.

3. session_compile: a manual build has no time limit and runs until it ends or is stopped. An automatic build is still stopped after 3 minutes, as a failure with the error "This automatic build was stopped after 3 minutes without finishing. Compile to build without a time limit; the Build Log shows how far it got."

4. Opening a folder or .tex with no settings yet (open_path and import): when no % !TEX program names an engine, a preamble loading fontspec, unicode-math, polyglossia, xeCJK or mathspec gives engine xelatex, and one loading luacode, luatexja or luaotfload gives lualatex. Hosts need no change for this.

The hosts can now drop their Install-specific use of `missing`.
done: A: LogItem (crates/texlocal-core/src/logparse.rs) has `explain: Option<&'static str>` and `fix: Option<Fix>` in place of `missing`. Fix is an enum (Install, AddPackage, Xelatex, ShellEscape) with a hand-written Serialize that produces {title, help, command, args, confirm?}.

A: EXPLAINED is a LazyLock table of 26 regexes matched against `short`. It covers undefined control sequence, undefined environment, missing $, extra or missing braces, runaway argument / paragraph ended, misplaced and extra alignment tab, \begin ended by another \end, missing \begin{document}, preamble-only commands, lonely \item, no line here to end, double super/subscript, option clash, can't write on file (Windows lock), file not found (graphics and others), missing .sty/.cls, emergency stop / no legal \end, undefined citation and reference, Unicode character, XeTeX-only packages, fontspec font not found, command already defined, and missing number. The old MISSING regex became the table's first entry.
A: the package map is data in syntax/catalog.json under `packages` (52 entries: every one listed in the task plus a few kin such as \midrule, align*, \Cref and \citet), read as CATALOG.packages.
A: compile.rs finish() drops an AddPackage fix when the main file already loads that package, reading the preamble with Facts::read.

Shared: Facts (analyze.rs) gained `packages` (from \usepackage and \RequirePackage, comments skipped) and `new_package` (the end of the line where the last \usepackage's argument ends, else \documentclass's). It has three callers: the engine guess, the fix pruning and session_add_package.

B: session_add_package in session/actor.rs reuses edit_project and texts_to_edit (session_replace's code path, through replace_in_files), so there is one path whether the main file is open or not. Tested in session/tests.rs: a_package_is_added_after_the_last_one_the_main_file_loads_unless_it_loads_it.

C: import.rs guessed_settings falls back to ENGINE_PACKAGES when no % !TEX program names an engine. The existing settings test is extended (renamed the_settings_guessed_are_what_a_tex_names_else_the_engine_its_packages_need).

D: process::drive takes Option<Duration>, and None means no timer. CompileManager::compile and Engine::compile take `auto`, and only an automatic build gets COMPILE_TIMEOUT. The log cap LOG_READ_MAX (16 MB, read from the tail) and the 1 MB stdout cap never depended on the timeout and still apply on their own; the comment was reworded to say so.

D test: compile/stubs.rs a_build_asked_for_has_no_time_limit pauses tokio's clock, advances it past twice the limit, then lets the stub finish. I confirmed it fails if the timeout is applied to manual builds. The existing timeout test now runs an automatic build.

Tests for A: logparse a_common_error_is_explained_and_offers_the_fix_that_usually_ends_it (explanations, package, XeLaTeX and shell-escape fixes, and the JSON shape) and stubs an_undefined_command_offers_its_package_only_while_the_main_file_doesnt_load_it (the pruning). The missing-file test now checks the Install fix.
docs/core-api.md updated for every command, field and behaviour above.
skipped: README.md is not updated. The new behaviour only becomes visible once the hosts show explain and fix, which is the next step, so the README change belongs there.

session_add_package inserts "\n\\usepackage{name}". In a main file that isn't open and has CRLF line ends, the new line therefore ends with a bare LF before the old CRLF. TeX doesn't mind, and the editor's next save writes one line ending throughout, so I didn't add per-file line-end handling.

Package-name fixes add the name only, never options. One map entry the task asked for, \sout -> ulem, changes \emph to underlining unless loaded with [normalem]. It is kept as specified; the hosts' step or a later one could add options to the fix if that is wanted.

Explanations aren't added to the `issues` or `live_issues` event lines. Hosts read them from build_finished's items and from session_issue / session_choose_issue answers, as the task specified for LogItem.
session_add_package doesn't check the package name it is given, because hosts pass the name from a fix the core produced.
checks: cargo fmt --all --check: passes. cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings: passes. cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast: everything passes except the four tests known to fail in this container (atomic a_save_that_cannot_complete_leaves_the_original_intact, import a_file_reports_what_it_would_land_on_and_never_overwrites_unasked, projects::files a_write_refused_says_so_in_a_sentence_naming_the_file_and_folder, syntax::render what_cant_be_drawn_is_an_error), which failed in every run. In one full-workspace run with --no-fail-fast, compile::stubs::a_build_failed_for_want_of_shell_escape_says_where_to_allow_it also failed once, and I didn't capture its message. It did not fail again in 6 runs on its own, 8 runs of the core lib suite or 5 more full-workspace runs. My guess, not confirmed, is a timing flake in the shell-stub tests, since that test's path through the code is unchanged apart from reading main.tex afterwards. The ffi tests (8) pass.
